calibration: cobra-v2.json's nl_behaviour rows (cb-11, cb-12, cb-13, cb-14, cb-15, cb-16, cb-17, cb-18, ci-43) were read before judging. Two findings govern this review. First, their queries carry no Go identifier and no path; cb-15 says 'the version flag' and cb-16 'the levenshtein distance', i.e. user-facing or domain vocabulary, never a symbol. Second, their grade-3 spans are whole declarations (ValidateRequiredFlags, InitDefaultVersionFlag, ld, IsAvailableCommand) - so a whole-function span is NOT per se a definition-instead-of-behaviour defect in this stratum. The precedent's real rule is that the grade-3 span must CONTAIN the deciding branch or condition. ci-43 shows the sub-span form for the case where it does not. The demotion in cq-32 follows from this rule, not from span size.

verdicts.note: All five spans read at the pinned revision and all resolve under CheckSpanCoverage (anchor inside [start_line,end_line], end_line within the file). command.go:1876-1885 is the whole commandNameMatches declaration including its doc comment, and it carries the deciding branch itself (if EnableCaseInsensitive -> strings.EqualFold, else s == t), so grade 3 is not a mere definition span. Verified independently that commandNameMatches has exactly two non-test call sites - command.go:770 in findNext and command.go:1508 in HasAlias - which are precisely the two grade-2 spans, so the reason 'the single comparison point' is true and not merely plausible. Stratum fits: the query names no identifier and no path and is the same shape as cb-16 ('where is the levenshtein distance computed').

command_win.go:30-41 is the complete preExecHook body and answers the question on its own: MousetrapHelpText != "" and mousetrap.StartedByExplorer() gate it, the text is printed, MousetrapDisplayDuration > 0 sleeps while 0 waits for return, then os.Exit(1). Grade 3 justified. command.go:1062-1065 verified as the ExecuteC call site and it does precede Find/Traverse (command.go:1088-1091), so 'before any command lookup happens' is accurate. Two observations that do not block release: (a) command_notwin.go:15-20 is widened beyond the span convention the draft states - the declaration alone is line 20, and lines 15-16 are the //go:build !windows constraint, not a doc comment. The widening is what makes the grade-1 reason true, but unlike cq-33 the draft does not declare it. Reviewer leaves the span as drafted and records the deviation here. (b) The grade-3 span sits in a //go:build windows file. I checked the ingest path (engine/ingest/walk.go uses a plain fs.WalkDir; core/parse/parser_go.go selects by extension and parses with go/parser) and it applies no build constraints, so command_win.go is indexed on darwin and the span is reachable. Note that preExecHookFn is declared in both command_win.go and command_notwin.go, so the two declarations compete during linking; that is a property of the repository, not a defect of this candidate.

Spans all exist and resolve. Two corrections. (1) shell_completions.go:42-46 (Command.MarkFlagFilename) was graded 3. It is a two-line wrapper that returns MarkFlagFilename(c.Flags(), name, extensions...) and determines no behaviour; the extension filter is decided at completions.go:352-364, where the BashCompFilenameExt annotation becomes ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt. cb-11 is the governing precedent and grades the analogous MarkFlagRequired 2 against ValidateRequiredFlags at 3. Demoted to 2; the candidate now has exactly one grade-3 span, the enforcement. (2) completions.go:54-94 is the entire ShellCompDirective const block, not a single constant; the reason now says so and names line 71 as the directive in question. The grade-3 span was read in full: lines 352-364 run from 'if flag != nil && flagCompletion {' through the close of the validExts block, and line 357 returns validExts with ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt - the behaviour the query asks about. Stratum fits.

command.go:1292-1300 is Commands() with its doc comment, and it holds the deciding branch ('if EnableCommandSorting && !c.commandsAreSorted { sort.Sort(commandSorterByName(...)) }'), so grade 3 is a behaviour span, not a signature. The 'in the help output' half of the question holds up: the usage template at command.go:560 binds '{{$cmds := .Commands}}' and ranges it for 'Available Commands', which I read to confirm the link. The hand-widened span command.go:1285-1290 is exactly as the draft declares it - line 1285 is the comment 'Sorts commands by their names.' and 1290 is the Less method - and AddCommand at 1302-1329 does clear commandsAreSorted at line 1327, so that reason is correct too. Both grade-1 tests were read and match their reasons. Not blocking, but for the dataset owner: the grade-3 span is byte-identical to one of the two grade-3 spans of ci-1861, which is a HOLDOUT row. Unlike cq-34 the two questions target different behaviour (dynamic subcommand discovery vs. ordering) and cq-33's decisive evidence - the sorting branch, the sorter type, the cache invalidation - is not what ci-1861 is about, so I release it. If the qualification forbids any grade-3 overlap between a dev row and a holdout row, this one goes with cq-34.

Not released as a dev row. The spans themselves are sound - I read all five and they resolve; command.go:879-881 is the deprecation print inside execute() and is a textbook behaviour span, and the grades are defensible. The blocker is elsewhere. cq-34's ONLY grade-3 span (command.go:879-881) is the ONLY grade-3 span of ci-1343, and ci-1343 is a HOLDOUT row whose question - 'Is there a way to customise entire deprecate message for a command' - is the same behaviour in another wording. A dev row whose complete grade-3 evidence set is identical to a holdout row's complete grade-3 evidence set for the same behaviour is not an independent development item: it makes the dev score a partial read-out of holdout evidence, which is the leakage family_id exists to prevent. The draft gives it a fresh family id (cobra-family-1eb5ff466e156979), which keeps Dataset.validate happy - families must not cross splits, and ci-1343 is holdout - but that is exactly what hides the problem instead of solving it. The reviewer's criterion applied here: reject when the whole grade-3 evidence set coincides with a holdout row's whole grade-3 evidence set AND both questions ask about the same behaviour. I invent no replacement span. The dataset owner can revive the row only by folding it into cobra-family-37f0353f67a41908 and moving it to split=holdout, which does not serve a dev qualification, or by re-drafting it around evidence ci-1343 does not use. Separately, the grade-3 reason claimed the print is 'the first thing execute() does'; it is not - command.go:875-877 is a nil-receiver check. The reason is corrected in `queries` so the record is accurate, but the correction does not lift the rejection.

All seven spans read and verified. command.go:611-621 is ErrPrefix with its doc comment and is the whole decision - own errPrefix, else recurse to the parent, else the literal "Error:" - so grade 3 is justified. Both use sites check out: command.go:1097-1101 is the lookup-failure branch in ExecuteC guarded by !c.SilenceErrors, and command.go:1126-1128 is the run-failure branch guarded by !cmd.SilenceErrors && !c.SilenceErrors, where the prefix is taken from cmd, not c - the reason's claim that it comes from the executed command rather than the root is correct, and TestRootAndSubErrPrefix (command_test.go:1145-1163) pins exactly that. The user_guide.md span and both test spans match their reasons. Stratum fits: the query says 'the prefix in front of a command's error message' and deliberately avoids naming ErrPrefix or SetErrPrefix.

not_released.reason: Its only grade-3 span, command.go:879-881, is the only grade-3 span of the holdout row ci-1343, which asks about the same behaviour. A new family id hides the dev/holdout evidence overlap rather than removing it. The spans are valid; the row is not an independent dev item. No replacement span was invented.
